words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some Arab philologists take the nearness as God’s greater power to act upon and control the person.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bunun mânası dediler, نَحْنُ أَمْلَكُ بِهِ وَأَقـْرَبُ إلَيْهِ فِي الْمَقْدِرَةِ عَلَيْهِ

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Other Arab philologists understand the nearness as greater knowledge of the whisper within a person.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da nefsindeki vesveseyi bilmekte daha yakın demektir dediler.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the reported interpreters do not mean nearness of God’s Essence; they choose nearness of power’s effect or of knowledge according to the discourse.
rows.anchor: Yani kurb-i Zât mânası anlayan olmadı, ancak kelâmın sevkine nazaran

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī reads the phrase as perfect divine knowledge: a vein can be screened from its owner, but nothing can screen God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: Fahr-ı Râzî bunu şöyle ifade etmiştir: “Allah teâlâ’nın ilminin kemâlini beyandır.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī also offers a power reading: God’s command acts in the person as blood flows through the veins.
rows.anchor: Emrimiz onda damarlarındaki kanın cereyânı gibi cereyan eder.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf calls the nearness metaphorical: God’s knowledge encompasses a person and every hidden state as though He were physically near.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf da şöyle der: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ mecazdır. Murad ona ilminin yakınlığı

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: He compares this expression with saying God is everywhere, while affirming that God is exalted above and transcendent from places.
rows.anchor: Nitekim ‘Allah her yerdedir’ denilir, hâlbuki Allah mekânlardan ecell ve münezzehtir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains the metaphor because literal nearness and distance apply spatially to bodies, whereas spatial proximity cannot be conceived of God.
rows.anchor: lügatta yakınlık ve uzaklık mekân ve mesafe itibariyle cismâniyyâtta hakikat olduğu

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî ile Ebussuud
rows.claim: They paraphrase the verse as knowing a person better than whoever is nearer to him than his jugular; essential nearness stands metaphorically for knowledge-nearness, which it causes.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî ile Ebussuud da bunu bir nükte ilâvesiyle hulâsa etmişler

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı supplies an elided comparison, “than whoever is nearer to him,” because a jugular vein cannot itself be the comparator for knowledge.
rows.anchor: Görülüyor ki bu ifadede مِ َّمنْ كَانَ اَقـْرَبَ اِلَيْهِ diye bir mufaddalun aleyh takdir olunmuştur.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible referent of the omitted “whoever” is the person himself; the vein then stands for the person, whom God knows better than he knows himself.
rows.anchor: O ya kendisinden kinayedir, bu surette “habl-i verîd”den murad kendi şahsı olup mâna onu kendisinden daha iyi biliriz demek olur

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “whoever” means the recording angels: they are nearer to the person than his vein, while God is nearer still, as the following passage suggests.
rows.anchor: Yahut zikrolunacak meleklerdir ki bu surette o hafaza

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Ālūsī remarks that expressions of the people of spiritual realization are difficult for those without such spiritual states.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî burada “ehl-i vahdetin kelâmı hâl sâhibi olmayanlar için zor anlaşılır şeylerdendir” demiştir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArabī calls the station of the Near One the highest station, essential for those who stumble, and describes its paradox as nearness containing distance.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî’nin Futûhât-ı Mekkiyye’sinin Esmâ-i Hüsnâ bâbında “Akreb” ism-i şerîfinde şu sözlerini nakledelim: حَضْرَةُ الأَْقْرَب أَعْلَى الْحَضَرَاتِ

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He says the servant is called “servant of the Nearer” or “servant of the Near,” citing God’s nearness and hearing, and the report that God descends to the lower heaven.
rows.anchor: Bu hazretin sâhibine ‘abdü’l-akreb’ ve ‘abdü’l-karîb’ denilir. Çünkü O azze ve celle bize habl-i verîdden akrebdir

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: For Ibn ʿArabī, God is with people wherever they are and nearer to them than themselves; human connection and every faculty ultimately depend on God.
rows.anchor: çünkü nerede olsak bizimle beraberdir, onun için Karîb, Akreb isimleriyle müsemmâdır. O bize bizden daha yakındır.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He contrasts the vein, merely a channel for life and blood, with God as the source of hearing, sight, standing, sitting, will, and judgment.
rows.anchor: Zira bizden habl-i verîdin gayesi diğer damarların hâli gibi hükm-i hayâtın mecrâsı ve kanların

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He says God legislated ways of nearness and made humans in His form; the servant is at once close as a counterpart and distant as an opposite.
rows.anchor: Sonra Allah teâlâ bizde de kendisine kurbu teşrî‘buyurdu. Çünkü biz O’nun sureti üzere mahlukları olduğumuz cihetle

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Through prescribed acts performed in humility, the servant draws near until God becomes his hearing, sight, and powers, as in the cited sacred report.
rows.anchor: yapmakla O onun sem‘i, basarı ve cemî‘-i kuvâsı olana kadar bu suretle kul

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He argues that the report’s pronoun still establishes the servant as himself; divine manifestation in the servant’s faculties does not mean the servant and God are identical.
rows.anchor: zamiri abde ircâ‘ile abdin aynını tesbit etmiş ve o, hüve hüve olmadığını isbat eylemiştir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He describes the cosmos as containing no other than God manifest through the stations of His beautiful names, while God remains transcendent and beyond them.
rows.anchor: Artık kevnde başka yok ancak O, esmâ-i hüsnâsının

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He says the law encompasses claimants and others.
rows.anchor: şeriat müddeîye ve gayr-i müddeîye âm oldu.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: He says people are resurrected according to intention and distinguished by their religion and school.
rows.anchor: kıyamet günü niyetine göre haşrolunur ve millet ve mezhebiyle seçilir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn ʿArabī affirms essential and active nearness, ending in the servant’s annihilation and unity; some of this discussion is difficult for spiritual outsiders.
rows.anchor: Görülüyor ki Şeyh beytinde bizzat kurba kāil olmuş ve kurb-i fiili anlatmış, sonunu da abdin fenâsıyla vahdete bağlamıştır.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reported descent to the lower heaven should indicate nearness of command, not place; the hadith does not say descent from the Throne.
rows.anchor: Hadiste nüzul var ise de Arş’tan kaydı yoktur

words: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı warns against turning unity of being into union: the verse opens by emphatically stating that humans are created, preserving the distinction between Creator and creature.
rows.anchor: Hâlık ve mahlûkun hakkı gözetilmek için evvelemirde وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ kasemiyle insanın mahlûkiyetini te’kîden tansis buyurmuştur.

words: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing Ibn al-Munayyir’s Kashshāf gloss, Elmalılı states his creed: nothing exists apart from God’s essence, attributes, and acts; God makes some acts the locus of others.
rows.anchor: olmak üzere Keşşâf hâşiyesinde İbn Müneyyir’in

words: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the world is God’s act and creation, including human acts attributed to people by compulsion or choice, as affirmed in 37:96; this is necessary monotheism for a believer.
rows.anchor: bütün âlem Allah’ın fiili, yani halkı olduğu gibi insanlar ve insanlara cebren ve ihtiyâren nisbet olunan fiiller de

words: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributes are neither identical with nor wholly other than the essence; acts are not their agent, and Creator and creature cannot be identical.
rows.anchor: aynı değildir, lâ-hüve velâ gayruhu’dur. Fiil de fâilin aynı olamaz. Hâlık ile mahluk hüve hüve müttehid olamaz.

words: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything belongs to God, but belonging to God does not make it God.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın olmayan hiçbir şey yoktur, hepsi Allah’ındır, lâkin Allah’ın olmak, Allah olmak değildir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearness preserves distinction: a messenger’s acts and strength may be attributed to the sender without making the messenger identical to the sender.
rows.anchor: resul, mürsilin aynı olmasını îcab etmez. Belki resûlün aynı sâbit olduğu hâlde kendisi de fiili de mürsilin olur.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant approaching through obligatory or supererogatory worship remains himself; divine power manifests through his faculties without making him God.
rows.anchor: kurb-i ferâizle ve gerek kurb-i nevâfille tekarrub etmiş olan abdin de aynı sâbit olmakla beraber

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spatial nearness entails an interval and is therefore a kind of distance; attributing place to God would make space greater than or partly outside His encompassing.
rows.anchor: mekânî yakınlık mutlaka arada bir faslı istilzam eder, aradaki fâsılanın büyüklüğüne küçüklüğüne göre mülâhaza olunur

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God transcends place and encompasses everything, Elmalılı explains nearness through attributes rather than essence to prevent imagining spatial proximity.
rows.anchor: kurb-i mekânî tevehhüm olunmamak için kurb-i zât ile değil

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a human is embodied and occupies space, describing God as near to the person’s essence could suggest spatial proximity; the metaphor rejects spatial, not divine essential, nearness.
rows.anchor: insanın zâtı bir cism-i mütemekkin olduğundan dolayı ona kurb-i zatî ile akrebiyet mülâhazası bir kurb-i mekânî îham edebilir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since metaphor is necessary here, exegetes select the safest meaning for the general public.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn, umum için en sâlim olan mânayı ihtiyar eylemişlerdir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In divine names and attributes, the intended end is their effects, such as glad tidings or warnings, even if “nearer” is read as essential nearness.
rows.anchor: sıfât ve esmâ-yı ilâhiyede matlub gāyâtı olduğuna göre akreb vasfı kurb-i zat ile tefsir edilse bile

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God is with people wherever they are has traditionally been explained as His knowledge; Elmalılı likewise allows knowledge or power as the sense of nearness here.
rows.anchor: ile tefsir olunduğu gibi buradaki akrebiyet de naklettiğimiz vechile ilim veya kudret yakınlığıyla tefsir olunmuştur.

words: وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ
وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı sees contextual cues as supporting both kinds of nearness, and asks why commentators state knowledge and power disjunctively; he finds no explicit answer.
rows.anchor: Bakılırsa bunun cem‘inde münâfat olmamalı, hem ilmi hem kudreti ile akrebiyet murad olunabilmeli idi, acaba niçin terdid ile söyleniyor?

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reason for the disjunction is that two metaphors or their implications may not be combined; Elmalılı thinks a representative metaphor or metonymy could allow it.
rows.anchor: kurb-ı zattan mecaz olmak hasebiyle iki mecazın, iki lâzımın bir arada cem‘i tecviz edilememek

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second proposed reason is that contextual cues support different senses: some indicate knowledge and others power, producing exegetical disagreement.
rows.anchor: siyak ve sibakda خَلَقْنَا، نَعْلَمُ، اِذْ يَتَلَقَّى، وَجَائَتْ، وَنُفِخَ gibi karînelerin bazısı yalnız ilmi bazısı da kudreti

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı favors combining the senses: knowledge is broader but does not entail power, whereas power entails knowledge; a power reading therefore also conveys knowledge.
rows.anchor: Kudret ise ilmi müstelzimdir. Kudret ile kurb murad edildiği takdirde

words: وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ
وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explicitly stating God’s knowledge of inner whispers, the added nearness clause points beyond knowledge alone; Elmalılı understands it as also implying power, care, kindness, and wrath.
rows.anchor: Onun için biz bundan yalnız ilmen kurb değil, lutf u inâyete kahr u gazaba da darb-ı mesel olabilen bir kurb anlıyoruz ki bu lâekal kurb-i kudrettir.

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Rāghib says qurb and distance are opposites used for place, time, relation, rank or honor, benefit, care, and power; his examples span the cited verses.
rows.anchor: Râgıb Müfredât’ında der ki: “Kurb ve bu‘d mütekābildirler. Kurb zamanda, mekânda, nisbette, huzve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the two recording officials as seated, one on the person’s right and the other on the left, writing the record.
rows.anchor: İki zabıt me’mûru zabıt tutarlarken: biri sağdan oturmuş biri soldan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He translates the verse to say that every word a person utters has a ready watcher beside him.
rows.anchor: Her ne söz atarsa mutlak yanında hazır bir gözcü vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death’s agonies arrive in truth and announce what the person kept fleeing.
rows.anchor: Ve ölüm sekerâtı hak ile geldikte, “işte” diye, “o senin kaçıp durduğun”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is blown, marking the promised day of warning.
rows.anchor: Ve Sûr üfürüldükte: ki işte o va‘îd günüdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul arrives accompanied by one who drives it and one who bears witness.
rows.anchor: Ve her nefis gelmiştir: beraberinde bir sevk me’mûru ve bir şâhid vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is told that he was heedless, but now the veil is removed and his sight is sharp.
rows.anchor: sen bundan bir gaflette idin: şimdi senden perdeni açtık, artık bugün gözün keskindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the companion as identifying the person beside him as present and ready.
rows.anchor: Ve karîni demiştir: “İşte bu yanımdaki hazır”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to cast into Hell every unbeliever who is stubborn and ungrateful.
rows.anchor: Atın atın cehenneme her nankör anûd

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı describes the condemned person as obstructing good, aggressive, troublesome, and unbelieving.
rows.anchor: hayra engel, haşarı işkilci kâfiri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned also took another deity alongside God; the two addressed are told to cast him into severe punishment.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın yanında başka ilâh tutmuştur, haydin ikiniz bir atın onu o şiddetli azab içine

words: مَآ أَطْغَيْتُهُۥ
وَلَٰكِن كَانَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۭ بَعِيدٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the companion’s defense as denying that he led the person astray and blaming the person’s own distant misguidance.
